chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Sind ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Yahya ibn Abi al-Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
In twenty dinars, [the khums is] half a dinar.

key_terms.دِينَار: Dinar, a gold coin used as currency

ai.seo_question: What is the khums amount for twenty dinars according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the zakat rate on gold dinars, establishing a rate of 2.5% (one-fifth of a dinar per twenty dinars), which aligns with the standard zakat calculation for wealth rather than the 20% khums on war booty. It reflects the early Shia scholarly tradition of deriving precise financial jurisprudence from the Imams, ensuring consistency with the broader Islamic legal framework regarding gold as a store of value. The narration underscores the importance of precise measurement in religious obligations, a key theme in Shia fiqh.
